title: Bonjour tout le monde!
oneGoal: Students will recognize and respond to basic French greetings

mindsOn.activity: Welcome circle with French greeting song and friendly wave gestures - teacher models 'Bonjour!' with big smile and wave
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students seem nervous → use more English transition; If engaged → continue full French
mindsOn.visualSupport: Large greeting cards with pictures, exaggerated facial expressions, welcoming gestures

activities: Greeting puppet show with different characters saying hello (~9 min)
Mirror greeting practice with gestures and facial expressions (~9 min)
Walk-around greeting game with simple hand signals (~9 min)
action.decisionPoint: If students hesitant to speak → emphasize listening and gestures; If ready to participate → encourage attempts at sounds
action.tprElements: Wave hello, nod yes/no, point to self, big smiles, hand to ear for listening

consolidation.activity: Goodbye circle where each student waves or says goodbye in their comfort zone
assessmentChecklist: Responds to 'bonjour' with gesture or sound
consolidation.decisionPoint: If tired → shorter sharing circle; If energized → extend with extra greeting song
consolidation.nonVerbalOptions: Wave, nod, smile, point to greeting card, thumbs up

emergencyBackup: Play greeting song repeatedly with simple TPR actions - teacher models, students copy
languageNote: Use 'hello' and 'say hello' alongside 'reconnaître' and 'répondre' - focus on welcoming feeling

title: Je m'appelle...
oneGoal: Students will understand and attempt to say their name in French

mindsOn.activity: Review yesterday's greetings with puppet friends, then puppet introduces itself with name - connects to previous lesson
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students remember greetings → build quickly to names; If need review → spend more time on 'bonjour'
mindsOn.visualSupport: Name tags with pictures, puppet pointing to itself, clear pointing gestures

activities: Puppet name introductions with dramatic pointing to self (~9 min)
Name card matching game with pictures (~9 min)
Pass the special name hat activity with gentle encouragement (~9 min)
action.decisionPoint: If students ready to speak → encourage 'je m'appelle'; If silent period → focus on understanding and pointing
action.tprElements: Point to self, tap chest, hold up name card, nod yes/no, thumbs up for recognition

consolidation.activity: Name celebration circle where students share comfort level - hold name card, point, or attempt phrase
assessmentChecklist: Points to self when hearing own name
Attempts name sharing in any form
consolidation.decisionPoint: If overwhelmed → just hold name cards and wave
consolidation.nonVerbalOptions: Hold name card up, point to self, nod when name called, thumbs up

emergencyBackup: Simple name song with pointing actions - teacher sings, students point to themselves when they hear their name
languageNote: Use 'my name is' alongside 'je m'appelle' - emphasize identity and belonging

title: Comment ça va?
oneGoal: Students will recognize feelings words and simple responses

mindsOn.activity: Greet students by name from yesterday, then show different feeling faces asking 'Comment ça va?' - builds on name recognition
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students respond to names well → add feeling check-in; If need more name practice → combine name/feeling
mindsOn.visualSupport: Large emotion face cards, exaggerated facial expressions, body language demonstration

activities: Feeling faces matching game with mirror practice (~9 min)
Emotion charades with simple gestures (~9 min)
Feeling weather report with thumbs up/down (~9 min)
action.decisionPoint: If students connect with certain emotions → spend more time there; If overwhelmed by choices → limit to happy/sad
action.tprElements: Big smile for 'content', sad face for 'triste', thumbs up/down, clapping for happy, slow movements for sad

consolidation.activity: Feeling circle where students show how they feel right now using cards, faces, or thumbs
assessmentChecklist: Responds to 'comment ça va' with gesture
consolidation.decisionPoint: If energy low → keep simple with happy/sad only
consolidation.nonVerbalOptions: Point to feeling card, make face, thumbs up/down, clap or move slowly

emergencyBackup: Simple emotion song with actions - students copy teacher's facial expressions and gestures
languageNote: Use 'how are you' and 'feeling' alongside curriculum terms - focus on emotional connection

title: Mes couleurs préférées
oneGoal: Students will identify and name basic colors in French

mindsOn.activity: Feeling check-in with color connections - 'I feel happy like yellow sunshine' - builds on emotion vocabulary from yesterday
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students remember feelings → connect to colors quickly; If need feeling review → slower transition
mindsOn.visualSupport: Brightly colored scarves, real colored objects, color-emotion connection cards

activities: Color scavenger hunt around classroom (~9 min)
Color sorting game with movement (~9 min)
Color dance with scarves and music (~9 min)
action.decisionPoint: If students drawn to specific colors → explore those more; If need movement → emphasize dance activity
action.tprElements: Point to colors, hold up colored objects, wave scarves, march to color stations, clap for color matches

consolidation.activity: Color preference sharing - students point to or hold their favorite color while teacher names it in French
consolidation.decisionPoint: If excited about colors → extend with color mixing talk
consolidation.nonVerbalOptions: Point to colors, hold colored objects, nod yes/no for color preferences, sort into groups

emergencyBackup: Simple color song with colored scarves - wave the color when you hear its name
languageNote: Use 'colors' and 'favorite' alongside 'couleurs préférées' - emphasize visual learning

title: Ma famille
oneGoal: Students will recognize family member words and relate to their own family

mindsOn.activity: Show family colors - 'My family's favorite colors' - connects yesterday's color learning to family introduction
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students eager to share families → encourage; If private → use example families only
mindsOn.visualSupport: Diverse family photos, simple family drawings, picture frames in different colors

activities: Family puppet show with different family types (~9 min)
Family picture sharing and pointing (~9 min)
Family movement song with actions (~9 min)
action.decisionPoint: If students want to share own families → provide time; If need structure → use puppet families primarily
action.tprElements: Point to family members, hug gesture for family love, counting family members on fingers, protective arm gestures

consolidation.activity: Family appreciation circle - students show or draw one family member they want to share
assessmentChecklist: Points to family members when named
Connects words to own family experience
consolidation.decisionPoint: If emotional about families → keep gentle and optional
consolidation.nonVerbalOptions: Point to family pictures, hold up drawings, nod for family recognition, hug gesture

emergencyBackup: Simple family song with pointing actions - point to different family members in pictures
languageNote: Use 'family' and 'mom/dad' alongside French terms - honor all family structures sensitively

title: J'aime, je n'aime pas
oneGoal: Students will express simple preferences using 'j'aime'

mindsOn.activity: Family preference sharing - 'My family likes...' using pictures from yesterday - builds on family vocabulary
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students remember family words → connect to preferences; If need family review → slower bridge
mindsOn.visualSupport: Clear preference cards with happy/sad faces, thumbs up/down visual cues, family activity pictures

activities: Like/don't like sorting game with food pictures (~9 min)
Preference movement game - jump for like, sit for don't like (~9 min)
Thumbs up/down preference survey (~9 min)
action.decisionPoint: If students love food topic → focus there; If restless → emphasize movement activities
action.tprElements: Thumbs up/down, happy/sad face expressions, jumping for likes, sitting for dislikes, clapping for favorites

consolidation.activity: Preference gallery walk - students point to pictures of things they like and give thumbs up
consolidation.decisionPoint: If engaged with preferences → extend discussion
consolidation.nonVerbalOptions: Thumbs up/down, point to pictures, nod/shake head, sort into like/don't like piles

emergencyBackup: Simple like/don't like chant with thumbs up/down actions for common items
languageNote: Use 'I like' and 'I don't like' alongside French - emphasize personal choice and opinion

title: Les nombres magiques
oneGoal: Students will recognize and count to 5 in French

mindsOn.activity: Count the things we like - 'I like 3 foods' using yesterday's preferences - connects counting to personal interests
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students remember preferences → use for counting; If need simpler start → just finger counting
mindsOn.visualSupport: Large number cards with dots, finger counting charts, number/object matching visuals

activities: Magic number finger song with actions (~9 min)
Number hunt around classroom with counting objects (~9 min)
Number dance - different movements for each number (~9 min)
action.decisionPoint: If students love songs → repeat number song; If kinesthetic learners → emphasize movement counting
action.tprElements: Hold up fingers for each number, march steps for counting, clap number patterns, point to counted objects

consolidation.activity: Magic number show - students demonstrate counting in their preferred way (fingers, objects, sounds)
consolidation.decisionPoint: If excited about numbers → preview number 6 briefly
consolidation.nonVerbalOptions: Hold up fingers, point to number cards, arrange counting objects, nod for correct numbers

emergencyBackup: Simple counting song with finger actions - count along with teacher using fingers
languageNote: Use 'numbers' and 'counting' alongside 'nombres' - emphasize math connection and magic feeling

title: Mon corps en français
oneGoal: Students will identify basic body parts in French

mindsOn.activity: Count our body parts - 'We have 2 hands, 5 fingers' - connects yesterday's numbers to body awareness
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students remember numbers → count body parts; If need number review → slower counting
mindsOn.visualSupport: Large body part picture cards, mirror for self-observation, simple body outline poster

activities: Body part Simon Says with gentle touches (~9 min)
Body part song with movements (~9 min)
Partner body part pointing game (~9 min)
action.decisionPoint: If students need movement → emphasize dance; If need calm → focus on gentle pointing
action.tprElements: Touch own head, wave arms, stomp feet, clap hands, point to body parts safely

consolidation.activity: Body appreciation circle - students point to one body part they're grateful for
assessmentChecklist: Points to correct body part when named
consolidation.decisionPoint: If wiggly → keep active with continued movement
consolidation.nonVerbalOptions: Point to body parts, nod yes/no for correct parts, gentle self-touches, follow simple movements

emergencyBackup: Simple body part song with pointing actions - touch each part as it's named
languageNote: Use 'body parts' alongside 'corps' - emphasize self-awareness and health connection

title: Dans ma classe
oneGoal: Students will name common classroom objects in French

mindsOn.activity: Use our hands to point to classroom things - connects yesterday's body part learning to environment exploration
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students remember body parts → use for pointing; If need review → practice pointing first
mindsOn.visualSupport: Picture cards of classroom objects, actual labeled items around room, pointing gesture cards

activities: Classroom scavenger hunt with picture matching (~9 min)
Object touching game with safe exploration (~9 min)
Classroom item sorting by use (~9 min)
action.decisionPoint: If students enjoy exploration → extend scavenger hunt; If need structure → focus on sorting
action.tprElements: Point to objects, pick up and show items, sort into containers, walk around classroom, touch safely

consolidation.activity: Classroom gratitude sharing - students point to one classroom item they're thankful for
consolidation.decisionPoint: If excited about classroom → discuss how items help learning
consolidation.nonVerbalOptions: Point to objects, hold up picture cards, nod for correct matches, arrange objects

emergencyBackup: Simple classroom object song with pointing to each item as named
languageNote: Use 'classroom things' alongside 'objets de classe' - emphasize learning environment connection

title: Écouter et comprendre
oneGoal: Students will demonstrate listening comprehension through actions

mindsOn.activity: Listening to classroom sounds - connects yesterday's classroom objects to active listening in the environment
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students ready for challenges → add complex listening; If need support → simple sound recognition
mindsOn.visualSupport: Listening ear gestures, sound picture cards, quiet hand signals

activities: French Simon Says with all learned vocabulary (~9 min)
Listen and do action stories (~9 min)
Sound recognition game with French words (~9 min)
action.decisionPoint: If students follow well → increase complexity; If overwhelmed → slower, clearer instructions
action.tprElements: Hand to ear for listening, follow action commands, stop and go movements, quiet tip-toe walking

consolidation.activity: Listening celebration - students show their best listening position and respond to simple French commands
consolidation.decisionPoint: If tired from listening → gentler, slower commands
consolidation.nonVerbalOptions: Follow actions, point to demonstrate understanding, nod yes/no, copy teacher movements

emergencyBackup: Simple listening song with clear actions - students copy teacher's movements
languageNote: Use 'listen' and 'show me' alongside French commands - emphasize comprehension over production

title: Sons et rythmes
oneGoal: Students will identify French sounds and rhythm patterns

mindsOn.activity: Listen to the rhythm of French words from yesterday - connects listening skills to sound patterns and music
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students love music → emphasize rhythm; If need quiet → focus on gentle sound patterns
mindsOn.visualSupport: Rhythm pattern cards, musical note pictures, French sound mouth position pictures

activities: French word rhythm clapping (~9 min)
Sound pattern echo games (~9 min)
French music and movement exploration (~9 min)
action.decisionPoint: If students connect with instruments → extend music time; If overstimulated → reduce volume and complexity
action.tprElements: Clap rhythm patterns, sway to French music, tap feet to beats, echo hand movements

consolidation.activity: Sound pattern sharing - students create their own simple rhythm with French words
consolidation.decisionPoint: If energized by music → continue with quiet French lullaby
consolidation.nonVerbalOptions: Clap patterns, move to music, point to sound cards, nod with rhythm

emergencyBackup: Simple French children's song with clapping - repeat rhythm patterns together
languageNote: Use 'songs' and 'music' alongside French terms - emphasize joy and sound awareness

title: Je peux parler français
oneGoal: Students will demonstrate confidence in using learned French vocabulary

mindsOn.activity: French sound confidence building - 'Listen to all the French sounds we know' - connects yesterday's sound awareness to speaking confidence
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students feeling confident → encourage more speaking; If hesitant → focus on celebration of understanding
mindsOn.visualSupport: All previous vocabulary cards, confidence building posters, celebration stickers

activities: French vocabulary show and tell with choice (~9 min)
Partner French conversation with pictures (~9 min)
French confidence building games (~9 min)
action.decisionPoint: If students ready to speak → provide more opportunities; If still in silent period → celebrate understanding
action.tprElements: Point proudly to vocabulary, give thumbs up for French attempts, clap for peers, confident standing posture

consolidation.activity: French celebration circle - students share one French word or phrase they feel proud of
consolidation.decisionPoint: If overwhelmed → keep sharing optional and celebratory
consolidation.nonVerbalOptions: Point to favorite French words, give thumbs up, nod with pride, hold up vocabulary cards

emergencyBackup: Confidence building song with all learned French words - celebrate every attempt
languageNote: Use 'I can' and 'French' alongside curriculum terms - emphasize capability and pride

title: Montrer ce que je sais
oneGoal: Students will demonstrate their French learning through chosen activities

mindsOn.activity: French confidence review - 'Show me what French you know' - builds on yesterday's confidence building
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students eager to share → provide multiple options; If nervous → emphasize choice and comfort
mindsOn.visualSupport: Choice cards showing different ways to share learning, celebration preparation materials

activities: Student choice demonstrations - drawing, acting, pointing (~9 min)
Peer appreciation and French sharing (~9 min)
French learning portfolio creation (~9 min)
action.decisionPoint: If students love choice → extend demonstration time; If need structure → provide clearer guidelines
action.tprElements: Point to learning achievements, give appreciation gestures, organize portfolio materials, celebrate peer success

consolidation.activity: Learning celebration and goal setting - students show pride in growth and think about future French learning
assessmentChecklist: Demonstrates French learning in chosen format
consolidation.decisionPoint: If emotional about progress → provide gentle encouragement
consolidation.nonVerbalOptions: Point to favorite learning, organize portfolio, give thumbs up to peers, nod with pride

emergencyBackup: Simple portfolio sharing - students point to their favorite French learning moments
languageNote: Use 'show' and 'know' alongside French terms - emphasize learning demonstration and choice

title: Célébrer notre français
oneGoal: Students will reflect on and celebrate their French learning journey

mindsOn.activity: French journey reflection - look at all our learning from yesterday's portfolios and celebrate growth
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students excited about progress → extend celebration; If overwhelmed → gentle acknowledgment
mindsOn.visualSupport: Learning journey timeline, celebration banners, achievement certificates

activities: French learning celebration activities (~9 min)
Appreciation circle for French growth (~9 min)
Future French goal setting (~9 min)
action.decisionPoint: If students want big celebration → provide party atmosphere; If prefer quiet → gentle acknowledgment
action.tprElements: Clap for achievements, give appreciation gestures, point to future goals, celebratory movements

consolidation.activity: French celebration finale - students share what they're most proud of in their French learning
assessmentChecklist: Sets positive intentions for future learning
consolidation.decisionPoint: If emotional about celebration → provide comfort and encouragement
consolidation.nonVerbalOptions: Point to proudest moments, give thumbs up, hug learning portfolio, smile with achievement

emergencyBackup: Simple celebration song with all learned French vocabulary included
languageNote: Use 'celebrate' and 'learning together' alongside French terms - emphasize community and achievement

title: Jeux de français
oneGoal: Students will practice vocabulary through games and play

mindsOn.activity: Game excitement building - 'Let's play with our French words!' - connects celebration energy to playful learning
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students high energy → active games; If calm mood → quiet games
mindsOn.visualSupport: Game choice cards with pictures, fun game props, playful visual cues

activities: French vocabulary bingo (~9 min)
French word movement games (~9 min)
French memory matching games (~9 min)
action.decisionPoint: If students love competition → tournament style; If prefer cooperation → team games
action.tprElements: Jump for bingo wins, dance for correct matches, clap for game success, move between game stations

consolidation.activity: Game reflection - students vote for favorite French game and suggest new game ideas
consolidation.decisionPoint: If energized → plan next game session
consolidation.nonVerbalOptions: Point to favorite games, thumbs up for preferences, organize game materials, smile with enjoyment

emergencyBackup: Simple French vocabulary charades - act out learned words for others to guess
languageNote: Use 'games' and 'fun' alongside French terms - emphasize joy in language learning

title: Histoires en français
oneGoal: Students will enjoy and respond to simple French stories

mindsOn.activity: Story excitement building using games from yesterday - 'Let's play story games!' - connects playful energy to narrative
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students love listening → longer stories; If restless → interactive stories
mindsOn.visualSupport: Picture storybooks, story props, comfortable reading corner setup

activities: Interactive French story with vocabulary (~9 min)
Story acting and movement (~9 min)
Story retelling with pictures (~9 min)
action.decisionPoint: If students captivated by story → extend reading time; If need movement → emphasize acting
action.tprElements: Act out story characters, point to story pictures, move like story animals, gesture story actions

consolidation.activity: Story sharing circle - students share favorite story moment using pictures or actions
consolidation.decisionPoint: If love stories → plan story extension activities
consolidation.nonVerbalOptions: Point to favorite story parts, act out characters, organize story props, nod with story enjoyment

emergencyBackup: Simple picture story with familiar vocabulary - point and respond to story elements
languageNote: Use 'story' and 'book' alongside French terms - emphasize narrative enjoyment and literacy connection

title: Chansons et danses
oneGoal: Students will participate in French songs and movement activities

mindsOn.activity: Story songs connection - 'Let's sing the story!' - connects yesterday's narrative experience to musical expression
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students love music → extend singing; If shy → gentle encouragement only
mindsOn.visualSupport: Song picture cards, dance movement cards, musical instruments display

activities: French children's songs with actions (~9 min)
Dance creation with French words (~9 min)
Musical French vocabulary games (~9 min)
action.decisionPoint: If students create amazing dances → showcase time; If need calmer activity → gentle swaying
action.tprElements: Dance with scarves, play rhythm instruments, march to music, create movement patterns

consolidation.activity: Musical sharing circle - students perform their favorite French song move or rhythm
consolidation.decisionPoint: If energized → continue with quiet music wind-down
consolidation.nonVerbalOptions: Dance or sway to music, play instruments, point to favorite songs, move scarves rhythmically

emergencyBackup: Simple French action song - copy teacher's movements while singing along
languageNote: Use 'songs' and 'dance' alongside French terms - emphasize physical and musical expression

title: Art en français
oneGoal: Students will create art while using French vocabulary

mindsOn.activity: Art movement connection - 'Let's paint our dance!' - connects yesterday's movement and music to visual creation
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students excited about art → provide variety of materials; If hesitant → simple options
mindsOn.visualSupport: Art supply picture cards, color words with art examples, creative process posters

activities: French color art creation (~9 min)
Vocabulary art projects (~9 min)
Art sharing with French descriptions (~9 min)
action.decisionPoint: If students absorbed in creating → extend art time; If finished quickly → add art appreciation
action.tprElements: Point to colors while creating, show art proudly, arrange art supplies, gesture art descriptions

consolidation.activity: Art gallery walk - students display and appreciate French-inspired artwork
consolidation.decisionPoint: If proud of art → plan display for families
consolidation.nonVerbalOptions: Point to art elements, arrange displays, nod appreciation, organize art supplies

emergencyBackup: Simple French color collage - arrange colored papers while naming colors in French
languageNote: Use 'art' and 'create' alongside French terms - emphasize creative expression and visual learning

title: Français partout
oneGoal: Students will discover French in their world beyond the classroom

mindsOn.activity: Art world connection - 'French art everywhere!' - connects yesterday's art creation to French culture in the world
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If students curious about world → explore more cultures; If overwhelming → focus on local French
mindsOn.visualSupport: World map with French regions, local French signs and labels, cultural picture cards

activities: French discovery hunt in school (~9 min)
Virtual French culture exploration (~9 min)
French in our community discussion (~9 min)
action.decisionPoint: If students find French everywhere → extend discovery; If need focus → choose one area deeply
action.tprElements: Point to French discoveries, walk around school searching, gesture excitement for findings

consolidation.activity: French world sharing - students share one place they've discovered French or want to find French
consolidation.decisionPoint: If excited about world → plan family French discovery homework
consolidation.nonVerbalOptions: Point to world locations, show discovery findings, nod with recognition, organize cultural materials

emergencyBackup: Simple French culture picture sharing - look at pictures of French-speaking places and point to interesting things
languageNote: Use 'everywhere' and 'world' alongside French terms - emphasize global connection and cultural awareness

title: Au revoir pour maintenant
oneGoal: Students will reflect on their French journey and look forward to continued learning

mindsOn.activity: French world reflection - 'We found French everywhere, including in our hearts!' - connects yesterday's discovery to personal growth
mindsOn.decisionPoint: If emotional about ending → focus on continuation; If excited → celebrate fully
mindsOn.visualSupport: Learning journey timeline, memory book pages, future learning possibility cards

activities: French learning memory creation (~9 min)
Future French goal setting (~9 min)
Celebration preparation and sharing (~9 min)
action.decisionPoint: If students want big celebration → provide special ceremony; If prefer quiet → gentle reflection
action.tprElements: Point to favorite memories, hug memory books, clap for achievements, gesture future excitement

consolidation.activity: French farewell circle - students share gratitude and excitement for future French learning
consolidation.decisionPoint: If tearful about ending → emphasize continuation and connection
consolidation.nonVerbalOptions: Point to grateful moments, hug friends, give thumbs up for future, wave goodbye lovingly

emergencyBackup: Simple gratitude circle with French words - each student says one French word they'll remember
languageNote: Use 'goodbye for now' and 'proud' alongside French terms - emphasize continuation and achievement
